parsed.explanation: Both operative frameworks criminalise same-sex intimacy (6 months–3 years; up to three years), with at least one documented enforcement instance: camp officials holding detainees on 'homosexuality' charges (2009). No trans-specific statute, protection, or trans-visitor case is recorded — an open question, not a safety. Social exposure is documented as high: a conservative majority reading same-sex relations as foreign, plus an aid body finding no protection against discrimination or violence for LGBTQ people. The administering state's courts and detention demonstrably operate (2005 political trial). Absent documented trans targeting or universal trans-specific measures, but with criminalisation, hostility and no recourse, thin-data extrapolation resolves to High Risk, below anchors with routine trans-visitor exclusion.

entry_documents.exposure: Document and marker rules not addressed by any source; birth-sex reading of a trans visitor's relationship could place them inside the criminal prohibition.
entry_documents.interaction: Outing at any check could feed into the same-sex criminal provision under whichever framework applies.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Administering state's security services, courts and detention operate on the ground (2005 trial of seven defenders); camp officials held prisoners on 'homosexuality' charges without court process (2009).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented; no trans-specific detention safeguards recorded.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: An outed visitor could move from social exposure into a criminal process run by either framework.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Which framework applies depends on locality; the administering state's jurisdiction reaches most of the ground. Facility placement rules for trans people not addressed.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Subnational variation means the harsher criminal provision applies everywhere; administration, not legality, differs.

care_services.exposure: Trans-specific medical care, medication and emergency-care treatment not addressed by any source.
care_services.interaction: An emergency could out a visitor with no documented non-discrimination safeguard in either framework.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Same-sex conduct criminalised under both frameworks; charge wielded by camp administration; same-sex relations framed as a foreign imposition. No trans-specific framing documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Movement's constitutional silence is claimed by a diplomat but is not decriminalisation and no statute decriminalises anything.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Social threat-framing plus a live criminal statute means outing carries legal, not merely social, consequence.

minors_guardians.exposure: A parent travelling with a minor faces the same criminalisation and social exposure; family-reading of a trans adult's status could prompt community scrutiny. Not specifically documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Community outing risk is amplified where same-sex relations are read as foreign and reports note no protection from violence.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Aid body states no protection for LGBTQ people against discrimination or violence; social reading of same-sex relations as foreign raises confrontation risk.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absent recourse, street hostility and any police involvement would leave an outed visitor without remedy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No protection mechanism, no trans-specific statute, no documented trans-visitor case; oversight shown only as criticism of a political trial (2005) without documented relief.
remedies_unknowns.protection: International monitoring exists but its 2005 intervention produced no documented outcome.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin, unremedied recourse means the criminal provision and social hostility govern the visit.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra has a universal trans-visitor exclusion register — an engineered, every-crossing exposure. This dossier lacks any trans-specific universal measure or documented trans-visitor processing, which lowers it relative to 0.35-A; but its criminal statute plus documented enforcement and zero recourse keep it in the same broad High-Risk vicinity.

Meridia documents a pattern of police extortion and overnight detention targeting transgender travellers. This dossier records no trans-targeted policing pattern — only same-sex criminalisation with one dated camp enforcement instance — so it sits above 0.25-B, while sharing its thin-recourse, criminalising structure.

Valdoria's harm is administrative friction — delay, questioning, no credible criminal pathway. Here a criminal prohibition with documented enforcement plus documented absence of any protection places severity a clear step above 0.55-A's registration holds, warranting a materially lower score.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is criminalisation without trans-specific definition: both the administering state (six months–three years, courts and detention demonstrably operating) and the movement's framework (up to three years, enforced in camps) prohibit same-sex intimacy, and nothing decriminalises it. A trans visitor whose relationship local birth-sex reading would cast as same-sex therefore stands inside a live criminal provision. Against this, no source documents a trans-specific statute, trans-visitor case, document/facility rules, or any protection mechanism; the diplomat's constitutional-silence claim is not law. Social exposure is documented as high — a conservative majority reading same-sex relations as foreign, with an aid body finding no protection from discrimination or violence. Tier-3 societal hostility with thin-to-no recourse, plus a latent but at least once-enforced criminal statute, produces High Risk without reaching the enforced-trans-targeting tier.
